sources.citation: Boone, Douglas; Boling, Mike; Silué, Lamine; Augustin, MaryAnne. 2000. Enquête sur les dialectes mandé nord de Côte d'Ivoire. Mandenkan 35: 17-71. (= Glottolog 'Blecke & Blecke 1999' 553972 and 87954; SIL ESR 2007-006 is the SIL edition of the same survey)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (group interviews sec. 4.1 pp. 30-31, intelligibility tests sec. 5.1.3, conclusion pp. 49-50 naming koro as one of five distinct languages). 'accent' only in the lay sense ('avec un accent différent', p. 30). No phonology, no tone, no word-stress statement; cites only Kashale 1997: 22-23 for Koro.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 1988. Eléments de phonologie du koyaga de Mankono (Côte-d'Ivoire). Mandenkan 16, 159 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SISTER LECT (Koyaga, koya1253, other member of the Koro-Koyaga node; mutually intelligible with Koro per Boone et al. 2000). Two-tone system with downstep (ch. II 'Les tons', p. 62ff.); a full-text search for stress/accent/intensit/proémin/prosod over the scanned finds no word-stress statement. Not a description of Koro.

sources.citation: Derive, Marie-José. 1985. Etude comparée des parlers manding de Côte-d'Ivoire. Mandenkan 10: 63-73 (summary of her 1983 thesis = Derive 1990, Peeters)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonological sketches only of julakan of Kong, julakan of Odienné, maukakan and worodugukakan; tonology H/L with lect-specific extra registers (p. 68). Koro not among the sketched lects and not named. Nothing on stress.
Family and vitality only; detailed entry paywalled. Nothing on phonology.
